author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a controller that works in Android but not a game
summary: Locate the layer where controller input stops by comparing Android navigation, emulator hotkeys, a PS2 pad test, and the target game's expected port or mode.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Ryōjōhen controller settings representing a device detected by the host but requiring the correct emulated port

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Find the last layer that still receives input

Use Android's game-controller tester to record the device descriptor, input source, buttons, axes, and hat values. In EmuCoreX, open the live input view before launching a game and confirm the same events arrive. Assign the device to PS2 Port 1 with a temporary clean map, then test a title screen that accepts pad input without requiring a loaded save.

Android menu navigation may come from keyboard-style key events and does not prove that a complete gamepad interface reaches the emulator. Do not remap every button until the device appears in the input monitor and is assigned to the active port. Also clear experimental hotkeys that can consume Start, Back, or face buttons before the virtual pad sees them.
Prepare four checkpoints for the same press

items: Android event tester confirms more than D-pad navigation keys.
Emulator hotkey list and active PS2 port captured.
Target title booted into a mode that accepts a controller.
Save screenshots of Android's event tester and EmuCoreX's input monitor with the same descriptor, buttons, axes, and source class visible.
Use a title screen that accepts Port 1 immediately, then test Start, one face button, both sticks, and a shoulder without loading a save.

blocks.text: Walk the press from Android to gameplay

items: 1. Confirm face buttons and axes appear as game-controller events, not only system keys.
2. Inspect whether the physical button is consumed by an emulator hotkey.
3. Open Port 1 and verify the exact logical device is assigned.
4. Run a neutral PS2 pad test before changing the target game.
5. If the pad test fails, remap one button and axis manually for diagnosis.
6. If the tester passes, check the game's expected port, player selection, and analog mode.
7. Disable one accessibility or remapping service only for a documented comparison.
8. Restart the title from a cold boot and repeat the same input path.

blocks.text: If Android sees events but EmuCoreX does not, inspect device mode, permissions, and the selected input backend. If the emulator monitor responds but the game does not, verify port, pad type, profile selection, and game-specific overrides. A second known-good title separates a mapping failure from a title that expects a different peripheral or controller slot.

From a cold app start, navigate the game's title screen, move both sticks through their full range, press every face and shoulder button, and open Start/Select functions. Background and resume the app, then reconnect the controller and repeat. The test passes only when one device owns Port 1 and no action is intercepted by Android navigation or emulator hotkeys.

items: Android exposes buttons and axes from one logical gamepad.
The PS2 tester displays the same intended functions.
The game responds in the correct player mode without sacrificing app navigation.
The evidence chain must identify the first layer that stops responding: Android event, emulator monitor, port assignment, binding, or game.
Re-pair or reconnect the device, cold-start EmuCoreX, and verify that Port 1 works before any menu-navigation key is consumed as a hotkey.

blocks.text: Where a detected device can still fail

items: Only D-pad and Enter work in Android: the device may be in keyboard mode.
Hotkeys fire but PS2 controls do not: separate hotkey and Port 1 bindings.
The tester passes but one game ignores input: check analog mode, port, or game state.
Input vanishes after backgrounding: repeat the device-reconnect procedure.

blocks.text: Return to the proven Port 1 profile

Unassign the temporary device, import the previously working Port 1 profile, and remove only the diagnostic map. Return the controller to its original hardware mode if it was switched between Android, XInput, or keyboard behavior. Do not clear application data; that would erase useful evidence and unrelated profiles without repairing the event path.
Android UI compatibility is a weaker test than gamepad events

Remote controls and compact keyboards can navigate Android while lacking analog axes, a gamepad source, or enough independent buttons for PS2 software. Record the actual event capabilities rather than relying on the product name. Device mode and descriptor can change after firmware updates or re-pairing, so repeat discovery before reusing an old profile.
